destinations.name: Cairo
destinations.summary: The pyramids and the new Grand Egyptian Museum are worth the trip, but expect relentless touts, thick traffic pollution, and a ticketing system that now wants your card, not your cash.
destinations.headline: Cairo in 2026: The Pyramids Deliver, the New Museum Impresses, and the Hustle Never Stops
destinations.body:
Cairo's headline attraction hasn't changed in 4,500 years, but how you pay to see it has. The Giza Plateau's general admission ticket for foreign adults now runs 700 EGP, with foreign students at 350 EGP and children under six free. That gets you into the open-air complex, the Sphinx enclosure, the Valley Temple of Khafre and the panoramic desert viewpoints, but not inside the pyramids themselves. Climbing into the Great Pyramid of Khufu costs an extra 1,000 EGP for adults on top of the entry fee, while Khafre's interior is 280 EGP and Menkaure's is 200 EGP. Nearly every official ticket window at major sites has also gone card-only, so a fistful of Egyptian pounds will not get you past the gate the way it used to.

The long-awaited Grand Egyptian Museum near the plateau opened to the public on November 4, 2025, and by December it had switched entirely to online, timed-entry booking, meaning walk-up purchases are no longer possible. Foreign adult admission runs about 1,500 EGP, roughly 30 US dollars at 2026 exchange rates, against 200 EGP for Egyptian nationals. It is the first time Tutankhamun's full treasure collection has been displayed together in one place, and it is genuinely the best reason to plan a Cairo trip right now.

Getting to and from the sites is where the honest friction starts. The Giza touts are as persistent as their reputation suggests: the fake 'free photo' handoff followed by a payment demand, the 'this entrance is closed, follow me' redirect, and the classic camel or horse ride that gets quoted low and then repriced tenfold once you're stranded on the animal are all still active scams tourists report running into daily. A firm, immediate no and walking straight to the official ticket kiosk avoids most of it.

Cairo's air is a separate, less avoidable problem. The city has repeatedly ranked among the most polluted major cities in the world through 2025, with annual PM2.5 levels around 39.9 micrograms per cubic meter, nearly eight times the World Health Organization's guideline, driven largely by an aging vehicle fleet stuck in near-permanent traffic congestion. Anyone with respiratory sensitivity should factor that into how many days they spend outdoors in the city center versus at the plateau, which sits on the edge of town with somewhat clearer air.

On safety, the US State Department keeps Egypt at a Level 2, 'Exercise Increased Caution,' rating, with a Do Not Travel warning limited to North and Middle Sinai and parts of the Western Desert, areas nowhere near standard Cairo or Giza itineraries. The embassy has issued periodic security alerts through early 2026 urging visitors to stay alert in public spaces and avoid demonstrations, standard advice for a major capital rather than a reason to cancel a trip. Money-wise, the Egyptian pound has been trading in the low-to-mid 50s against the dollar through 2026 while domestic inflation sits around 14 percent, so prices quoted in pounds can feel like they're moving under your feet even as your dollars or euros still stretch reasonably far.
destinations.what_great:
The Grand Egyptian Museum is the real headline here. Since opening on November 4, 2025, it has finally given Tutankhamun's roughly 5,000-piece collection a single dedicated home, something Cairo never had before, and it sits within sight of the pyramids themselves. The plateau's 700 EGP general admission still buys access to the Sphinx, the Valley Temple and unobstructed views of all three main pyramids, and the desert setting at sunrise or late afternoon, before the midday heat and haze peak, remains one of the most genuinely awe-inducing experiences in travel.

The currency situation, while volatile, currently favors visitors carrying dollars or euros, and museum and monument admission prices, even after 2026 increases, are still inexpensive by major-capital standards once converted. Cairo's density also means a huge amount, from Islamic Cairo's mosques to Coptic Cairo's churches to Khan el-Khalili's bazaar, sits within a relatively compact, walkable-adjacent radius once you're clear of the plateau traffic.
destinations.what_ruined:
The nickel-and-diming is real and it's now unavoidable rather than optional. General plateau admission does not include entry to any pyramid interior, so a family wanting to actually go inside Khufu's chamber is paying 700 EGP plus 1,000 EGP per adult, and virtually every official ticket point has shifted to card-only payment, so travelers who show up assuming Egypt is a cash economy get turned away at the window.

Tout pressure at Giza specifically, the fake gift handoff, the redirect to a 'closed' entrance, the camel ride that balloons in price once you're on the animal and away from the crowd, is persistent enough that most visitors end up either hiring an official guide just to run interference or spending real energy saying no on repeat. Layer on Cairo's traffic, which is a genuine source of stress and delay across the city, and pollution levels that put it among the most polluted major cities measured in 2025, and the qualitative cost of a Cairo trip is higher than the ticket prices alone suggest.
tips: Book Grand Egyptian Museum tickets online in advance only; walk-up purchases stopped when the museum moved to online-only, timed-entry ticketing in December 2025.
Bring a physical credit or debit card for Giza and museum admission; official ticket windows at major sites have gone largely card-only and often will not accept cash pounds.

Budget separately for pyramid interiors: 700 EGP covers general Giza admission, but entering Khufu's Great Pyramid costs an additional 1,000 EGP per foreign adult, Khafre is 280 EGP extra and Menkaure is 200 EGP extra.

Decline any unsolicited 'free' photo, gift or camel-ride offer at the plateau immediately and firmly; the price-switch scam where a cheap-quoted camel or horse ride balloons tenfold once you're mounted is still commonly reported.

Apply for the e-visa only at the official visa2egypt.gov.eg portal; Egypt raised e-visa fees in 2026 to 30 dollars for single entry and 65 dollars for multiple entry, and third-party sites will overcharge on top of that.
Visit between October and March for daytime temperatures around 14 to 22 Celsius; summer months regularly push past 34 to 40 Celsius and coincide with worse smog days in the city center.

guide.title: Cairo Practical Guide: Getting Around, When to Go, and Where to Stay
guide.summary: How to navigate Cairo's metro and traffic, when the weather and crowds actually work in your favor, and where to base yourself for the pyramids, the museum and the old city.
guide.body:
Cairo's metro is the fastest and cheapest way to cross the city, avoiding the traffic that clogs most surface streets for hours a day. As of the March 2026 fare increase, a ride of up to 9 stations costs 10 EGP, up to 16 stations is 12 EGP, up to 23 stations is 15 EGP, and anything longer tops out at 20 EGP, payable with a single paper ticket or a rechargeable contactless card tapped at the gate. For the Giza Plateau itself, which sits outside easy metro reach, ride-hailing apps like Uber and Careem are the more reliable and scam-resistant option over hailing a street taxi, where drivers claiming a 'broken meter' remain one of the most common tourist complaints in the city.

October through March is the peak window for a reason: daytime temperatures sit in a comfortable 14 to 22 Celsius range, though hotel prices and crowds climb accordingly. The shoulder months of March to May and September to November offer a middle ground, with temperatures around 23 to 29 Celsius, thinner crowds, and lower rates. Summer, from roughly May through September, brings dry desert heat that regularly clears 34 Celsius and can exceed 40 Celsius at midday, which combines poorly with the plateau's shadeless open terrain and the city's traffic-driven smog.

Zamalek, the leafy island neighborhood on the Nile, is the most common base for visitors who want quieter streets and easy river access, while Downtown Cairo and Garden City sit closer to the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir and Khan El-Khalili bazaar in Islamic Cairo. Staying near Giza itself cuts commute time to the pyramids and the new museum but puts you farther from the old city's mosques, churches and market streets. For money-saving moves, carry a card for all official admissions since cash is increasingly refused at ticket windows, keep smaller Egyptian-pound cash on hand specifically for baksheesh, roughly 20 to 50 EGP for informal help at smaller mosques or Coptic churches, and confirm any e-visa purchase is going through the official government portal rather than a marked-up third-party reseller.

rating_rationale.overall: The Grand Egyptian Museum plus the pyramids is a legitimately world-class pairing, but constant tout pressure and card-only ticketing friction keep it from a perfect score.
rating_rationale.safety: US State Department rates Egypt Level 2 with Cairo outside the Do Not Travel zones, but periodic embassy security alerts and dense petty-crime/scam pressure at tourist sites warrant real caution.
rating_rationale.value: Admission prices are still modest by global capital standards, but 2026 fee hikes across e-visas, metro fares and site tickets, plus separate interior-access charges, add up faster than the headline numbers suggest.

facts_checked: Grand Egyptian Museum opened to the public on November 4, 2025, and moved to online-only, timed-entry ticketing (no walk-up purchases) by December 2025.
Grand Egyptian Museum foreign adult admission is approximately 1,500 EGP (about 30 USD at 2026 rates); Egyptian nationals pay 200 EGP.
Giza Plateau general admission is 700 EGP for foreign adults and 350 EGP for foreign students; children under 6 are free.
Entering the Great Pyramid of Khufu costs an additional 1,000 EGP for foreign adults (500 EGP for students), on top of the 700 EGP plateau entry.
Khafre pyramid interior access is an additional 280 EGP; Menkaure pyramid interior access is an additional 200 EGP.
Most official Egyptian tourist-site ticket windows have shifted to card/online payment, with cash increasingly not accepted at major site ticket booths.

Common Giza-area tourist scams include the unsolicited 'free photo/gift then demand payment' trick, the fake 'closed entrance' redirect, and camel/horse rides quoted cheap then repriced far higher after the ride.
Cairo ranked among the world's most polluted major cities in September and October 2025, per IQAir; 2024 annual PM2.5 averaged 39.9 micrograms per cubic meter (AQI ~111), about 8x the WHO guideline.
Road transport accounts for roughly 33% of Cairo's PM2.5 pollution, with an aging vehicle fleet contributing heavily to traffic congestion.

US State Department rates Egypt Level 2, 'Exercise Increased Caution,' with Do Not Travel guidance limited to Northern/Middle Sinai and parts of the Western Desert; Cairo tourist sites fall outside those zones.
US Embassy Cairo issued periodic security alerts through early-to-mid 2026 advising heightened public-space caution.
Egypt raised tourist e-visa fees in 2026 to 30 USD for single entry (up from 25 USD) and 65 USD for multiple entry (up from 60 USD); single-entry visas are valid 3 months for a 30-day stay.
Cairo Metro fares increased March 27, 2026: 10 EGP (up to 9 stations), 12 EGP (10-16 stations), 15 EGP (17-23 stations), 20 EGP (24+ stations).
USD/EGP exchange rate traded roughly in the low-to-mid 50s (around 51-54 EGP per dollar) through early-to-mid 2026.
Egypt's annual inflation rate was about 14.3% in June 2026, down slightly from 14.6% in May 2026.
Best weather window for Cairo is October through March, with daytime temperatures around 14-22C (57-72F); summer (May-September) daytime highs commonly exceed 34C and can pass 40C (104F).

destinations.name: Cape Town
destinations.summary: Cape Town combines Table Mountain, Cape Peninsula beaches and the Winelands with a food scene now anchored by Time Out Market and the V&A Waterfront, but a clear-eyed visitor needs real facts on crime hotspots, airport taxi scams and the city's power and water history before booking.
destinations.headline: Cape Town 2026 Travel Guide: Table Mountain, Wine Country and Beaches, Plus the Safety and Power Facts Visitors Actually Need
destinations.body:
Cape Town's signature draw remains Table Mountain, reached by the Aerial Cableway for R475 per adult and R230 per child on a return ticket booked online, roughly 10 percent cheaper than buying at the ticket office. From the summit plateau, visitors get panoramic views over the city bowl, Table Bay and the Atlantic seaboard suburbs of Camps Bay, Clifton and Sea Point, all considered safe to walk in daylight. A short drive out of the city opens onto the Cape Winelands, where a full day guided tour through Stellenbosch and Franschhoek runs about R1,400 to R2,500 per person, roughly 80 to 145 US dollars, including transport, tastings and lunch, typically departing Cape Town around 9am and returning by early evening.

The food scene has matured well beyond wine country. The V&A Waterfront now hosts more than 80 restaurants, bars and cafes, including the newer Time Out Market Cape Town, which features Cape Malay focused Barakat, the shisanyama inspired MLILO and a ramen outpost from World's 50 Best nominated FYN. Across town, the Old Biscuit Mill's Neighbourgoods Market, running since 2006, has grown into a Saturday institution with dozens of food vendors and live music.

Safety requires more nuance than blanket warnings suggest. Township areas such as Nyanga and Khayelitsha, along with parts of the Cape Flats, see genuinely high crime rates and are not suited to independent tourist visits outside a reputable guided tour, while gang violence there mostly stays within local communities rather than spilling into tourist zones. The roads immediately around Cape Town International Airport are a specific hotspot, and the US Embassy issued a warning in February 2026 about fake taxi operators targeting new arrivals there, recommending app booked rides picked up only from the designated rank. Within the city, locals generally avoid walking alone at night anywhere except the V&A Waterfront promenade, defaulting to Uber instead.

On infrastructure, Eskom's April 2026 winter outlook, covering April through August, removed the Western Cape from load shedding schedules entirely, following a run of 341 consecutive days without outages nationally, a marked change from the rolling blackouts of prior years. Cape Town's other defining crisis, the 2015 to 2018 drought that nearly triggered Day Zero water shutoffs when the Theewaterskloof Dam fell to roughly 10 percent capacity, is now history: the dam recovered to 100 percent by October 2020 and normal water use has continued since, though the episode still shapes local attitudes toward conservation.
destinations.what_great: Cape Town delivers a genuinely rare combination for one city: a cable car ride to a flat-topped mountain summit with sweeping ocean views, Blue Flag beaches at Camps Bay and Clifton within a 15 minute drive of downtown, and a Winelands day trip through Stellenbosch and Franschhoek that ranks among the most scenic wine regions anywhere. The dining scene has caught up too, with Time Out Market Cape Town and the long running Neighbourgoods Market giving visitors an easy, low stakes way to sample Cape Malay, African and international cooking side by side, and the current absence of scheduled load shedding means none of it is likely to be interrupted by a power cut.
destinations.what_ruined: The honest friction is that safety in Cape Town is genuinely uneven rather than overhyped or underhyped. Tourist zones like the V&A Waterfront, Camps Bay and Sea Point are low risk in daylight, but the roads around the airport are an active hotspot for fake taxi scams serious enough that the US Embassy warned about them in February 2026, and township areas like Khayelitsha and Nyanga carry real crime risk that makes independent visits unwise. Layer on the fact that almost nobody, local or visitor, walks alone at night outside the Waterfront, and a trip that looks purely scenic in photos requires constant low level logistics planning around transport that a first timer may not expect.
tips: Table Mountain Aerial Cableway online return tickets cost R475 for adults and R230 for children, about 10 percent cheaper than buying at the ticket office on the day.
Eskom's April 2026 winter outlook, covering April through August, took the Western Cape off load shedding schedules entirely after 341 consecutive days without outages nationally.

The US Embassy warned in February 2026 about fake taxi operators targeting arrivals at Cape Town International Airport, so book rides only through an app and collect them from the designated pickup point.

US, UK, EU, Canadian and Australian passport holders can enter South Africa visa free for up to 90 days, provided the passport is valid at least 30 days beyond the exit date and has two consecutive blank visa pages.

A guided full day wine tour to Stellenbosch and Franschhoek typically costs R1,400 to R2,500 per person, roughly 80 to 145 US dollars including transport, tastings and lunch, departing Cape Town around 9am and returning by early evening.

guide.title: Cape Town Practical Guide: Getting There, When to Go and What to Budget
guide.summary: A practical rundown of when to visit, where to base a stay, what to budget and which parts of the city are worth skipping.
guide.body:
Most international visitors fly into Cape Town International Airport, where the airport road corridor is a known crime hotspot and app booked transport from the official rank is the safer default over hailing a cab curbside. Cape Town's seasons run opposite to the Northern Hemisphere: the dry summer from November through March brings the most consistent sunshine and the busiest, most expensive crowds, especially in January, while winter from June through August is cooler and wetter, with 60 to 100mm of rain a month from Atlantic cold fronts. Autumn, March through May, is widely considered the best value window, with warm settled weather around 18 to 26 degrees Celsius, calmer winds and lighter crowds than peak summer.

For a first stay, Sea Point, Green Point and the V&A Waterfront offer walkable, well lit bases close to restaurants and within daylight walking distance of the Waterfront's shops and markets, while Camps Bay and Clifton suit travelers prioritizing beach access over city center convenience. Budget for the Table Mountain cableway at R475 per adult return, a Winelands day tour at R1,400 to R2,500 per person, and app based rides for essentially all after dark movement, since walking alone at night is not standard practice even for residents outside the Waterfront promenade. Must do experiences include the cableway or a Platteklip Gorge hike up Table Mountain, a Stellenbosch and Franschhoek wine day, and a stop at Neighbourgoods Market or Time Out Market Cape Town for a single meal sampling multiple kitchens. What to avoid: independent, unguided visits to Cape Flats townships like Khayelitsha or Nyanga, curbside taxi touts at the airport rather than app booked or official rank rides, and assuming current load shedding relief is permanent, since South Africa's grid has reversed course before.

rating_rationale.overall: Table Mountain, the Winelands and a genuinely strong food scene combine into one of the most complete city trips in Africa, held back only by the extra planning safety requires.
rating_rationale.safety: Core tourist areas are safe in daylight and load shedding risk is currently low, but airport taxi scams and no-go township areas mean visitors cannot treat the city like a low vigilance destination.
rating_rationale.value: A R475 cableway ticket and a full day Winelands tour for under 150 US dollars make premium experiences accessible, though app based transport costs add up for visitors avoiding walking at night.

facts_checked: Table Mountain Aerial Cableway online adult return ticket price R475 and child return R230, ticket office about 10 percent more expensive, capetrek.co.za

Eskom's April 2026 winter outlook removed the Western Cape from load shedding schedules for April through August 2026, following 341 consecutive days without load shedding, capetownetc.com and ourpower.co.za
US Embassy warning issued February 2026 about fake taxi scams targeting arrivals at Cape Town International Airport, travelsafe-abroad.com
Township areas including Nyanga, Khayelitsha and parts of the Cape Flats carry high crime rates and are not suited to unguided tourist visits, travellersworldwide.com and thebrokebackpacker.com

US and UK citizens, along with roughly 100 other nationalities, receive visa free entry to South Africa for up to 90 days, with a passport valid 30 days beyond exit and two blank visa pages required, visaverge.com
Guided full day Stellenbosch and Franschhoek wine tours cost roughly R1,400 to R2,500 per person including transport, tastings and lunch, privatetourscapetown.com and thenwewalked.com

Cape Town's Theewaterskloof Dam fell to about 10 to 11 percent capacity during the 2018 Day Zero drought crisis and recovered to 100 percent by October 2020, Wikipedia Cape Town water crisis and globalcitizen.org
Cape Town's dry season runs November to March and its wetter winter season runs June to August with 60 to 100mm of rain monthly, weather2travel.com and discover-capetown.com
The V&A Waterfront hosts more than 80 restaurants, bars and food markets including the newer Time Out Market Cape Town, waterfront.co.za and timeout.com

destinations.name: Cusco
destinations.summary: Cusco is the Inca capital turned Andean crossroads city, prized for its stonework, Sacred Valley access and food scene, but a 2026 visit now means navigating stricter Machu Picchu ticketing, real altitude risk and an unpredictable protest corridor along the rail line.
destinations.headline: Cusco and Machu Picchu in 2026: new ticket rules, altitude risk and rail protests travelers need to plan around
destinations.body:
Cusco remains one of South America's most architecturally dense cities, built directly on and around Inca foundations. Qorikancha, once the empire's richest religious site with gold sheathed walls, still shows Inca stonework fused with a colonial church built on top of it. Sacsayhuaman, the fortress complex above the city, has walls made from stones weighing up to 200 tons fitted without mortar. From Cusco, the Sacred Valley opens up toward Pisac and Ollantaytambo, the latter a still inhabited 15th century town with its original stone streets and water channels intact, and it functions as the main jumping off point for the train to Machu Picchu.

Getting into Machu Picchu itself changed materially for 2026. The Ministry of Culture set the daily cap at 4,500 visitors for most of the year, rising to 5,600 on a defined set of high demand dates including January 1, April 2 through 5, June 19 through November 2, and December 30 and 31. Standard circuit tickets for foreign adults run 152 soles, about 40 US dollars, while tickets bundled with Huayna Picchu or Machu Picchu Mountain access cost 200 soles, about 53 dollars, and those mountain add ons are capped separately at 200 and 400 climbers per day. Exiting the archaeological site now forfeits the rest of that day's ticket entirely, and Inca Trail permits no longer include citadel entry, so trekkers must buy the Machu Picchu ticket as a separate line item.

Cusco's altitude sits close to 3,400 meters, and the thinner air, roughly 35 percent less oxygen per breath than at sea level, causes real acute mountain sickness in a large share of arrivals regardless of fitness level, with headaches, dizziness and shortness of breath typically surfacing in the first one to two days. The city's food scene has kept pace with its tourism growth, with Gaston Acurio's Chicha and the contemporary Andean menu at MAP Cafe inside the Museo de Arte Precolombino anchoring a wider push into native Andean ingredients alongside standards like alpaca, cuy and lomo saltado.

The other 2026 wrinkle is transport reliability. A dispute between rival bus concessionaires over the Aguas Calientes to Machu Picchu shuttle contract led to rail and road blockades in September and November 2025 that stranded roughly 900 tourists and required overnight evacuation trains for about 1,400 more, and separate large scale protests in Lima in January 2026 disrupted travel more broadly. The underlying conflict was unresolved as of early 2026, meaning the Ollantaytambo rail corridor can still be blocked with little warning.
destinations.what_great: Cusco delivers a rare combination for a single trip: dense, walkable Inca and colonial architecture in the city itself, a Sacred Valley of living Inca towns like Ollantaytambo and terraced sites like Pisac within an easy day trip, and the payoff of Machu Picchu at the end of it. Cusco's dining scene has matured well beyond tourist fare, with serious Andean and Peruvian kitchens like Chicha and MAP Cafe drawing praise independent of the ruins next door, and the surrounding valley supports everything from easy walks to serious high altitude trekking.
destinations.what_ruined: The honest friction is threefold. First, altitude sickness is not a fringe risk, most arrivals feel some effect from Cusco's 3,400 meter elevation within the first day or two, and skipping acclimatization before a demanding trek is a common way to cut a trip short. Second, the 2026 Machu Picchu system is stricter and less forgiving than in past years, no same day re-entry, mandatory separate tickets even for Inca Trail hikers, and mountain permits that sell out four to five months ahead in peak season, which punishes anyone booking casually. Third, the rail corridor into Aguas Calientes has been an active protest flashpoint since late 2025 over a bus contract dispute, and travelers who build no slack into their itinerary risk being stranded or missing entry entirely if blockades recur.
tips: Standard Machu Picchu entrance tickets for foreign adults cost 152 soles, about 40 US dollars, while tickets including Huayna Picchu or Machu Picchu Mountain access cost 200 soles, about 53 dollars, per the official 2026 booking guide.

The Ministry of Culture opens ticket sales roughly four months ahead of each date at www.machupicchu.gob.pe, and peak season dates in June through August have sold out within one to two weeks of release, so booking two to three months ahead is recommended for that window.

Round trip PeruRail or IncaRail economy class tickets between Ollantaytambo and Aguas Calientes start around 80 US dollars, with mid tier Vistadome or 360 service running 140 to 180 dollars, and departures from Cusco or Poroy cost 30 to 50 dollars more than boarding at Ollantaytambo.

Cusco sits at about 3,400 meters, roughly 35 percent less oxygen per breath than sea level, and health guides recommend two to three days of light activity before any strenuous trek or the Inca Trail to reduce acute mountain sickness risk.

A recurring scam involves people posing as plainclothes police who ask to inspect cash for counterfeit bills, real Peruvian police do not request this, and travelers are advised to use official or app based taxis such as Uber or InDriver and agree on fares before the ride starts.

Citizens of the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, the EU and Japan do not need a visa for tourist visits and are typically granted stays up to 90 days, though Peru's 2026 entry system requires visa exempt travelers to complete electronic registration at least 72 hours before arrival.

guide.title: Cusco and Machu Picchu: a 2026 planning guide
guide.summary: How to sequence altitude, tickets and trains for a Cusco and Machu Picchu trip in 2026, and what to budget and avoid along the way.
guide.body: Most visitors fly into Cusco's Alejandro Velasco Astete airport from Lima, then base in the historic center for the first two to three days purely for altitude acclimatization before attempting the Sacred Valley or any trek. The dry season from May through September is the most reliable weather window and the busiest, while late April to May and September to early October offer a calmer, still mostly dry sweet spot; January and February bring the heaviest rain and some trail closures for maintenance, so they are the months to avoid for trekking specifically. From Cusco, most travelers stage through Ollantaytambo, taking a bus or colectivo there before boarding a PeruRail or IncaRail train to Aguas Calientes, the town at the base of Machu Picchu, since no road reaches the ruins directly. Budget for lodging in central Cusco, a separate one or two night stay near Aguas Calientes if doing an early entry, the entrance ticket itself, and the round trip train fare, which together typically run several hundred dollars per person once mountain permits or premium train classes are added. The must do sequence is Qorikancha and Sacsayhuaman in the city, at least one Sacred Valley town such as Ollantaytambo or Pisac, and Machu Picchu itself, ideally with an early entry slot booked months ahead. What to avoid: skipping acclimatization days before strenuous altitude activity, assuming same day walk up tickets exist at Machu Picchu (they do not, all entry is pre booked), and building a tight itinerary that leaves no buffer for possible rail disruptions on the Ollantaytambo to Aguas Calientes line, which has seen protest related blockades in the 2025 to 2026 season.

rating_rationale.overall: The combination of Inca architecture, Sacred Valley access and Machu Picchu remains genuinely exceptional, but the new stricter ticketing and mandatory circuit system make it less of a spontaneous destination than it used to be.
rating_rationale.safety: Altitude sickness affects most visitors to some degree, petty scams targeting tourists (fake police, inflated taxi fares) are well documented, and the Ollantaytambo rail corridor has seen real protest blockades stranding tourists as recently as the 2025 to 2026 season.
rating_rationale.value: Entrance tickets and mountain permits are moderately priced by international standards, but mandatory separate tickets for Inca Trail hikers, rising train fares and the need to book trains and tickets months ahead push the effective cost and planning burden higher than a simple one price entry fee suggests.

facts_checked: Machu Picchu daily visitor cap of 5,600 on high season dates (Jan 1, Apr 2 to 5, Jun 19 to Nov 2, Dec 30 to 31, 2026) and 4,500 the rest of the year, standard foreign adult ticket 152 soles/$40 and premium mountain tickets 200 soles/$53, no same day re-entry, Inca Trail permits no longer include citadel entry, Huayna Picchu capped at 200/day and Machu Picchu Mountain at 400/day (Agencia Andina; machupicchu.org 2026 booking guide)

Machu Picchu ticket booking window opens about four months ahead via www.machupicchu.gob.pe, peak season (June to August) tickets have sold out within one to two weeks of release (theonlyperuguide.com; bushop.com Machu Picchu Booking Timeline 2026)

PeruRail/IncaRail round trip economy fares from Ollantaytambo start around $80, mid tier Vistadome/360 service runs $140 to $180, Cusco/Poroy departures cost $30 to $50 more than Ollantaytambo, high season booking recommended 60 to 90 days ahead (machupicchu.org train cost guide; turismoliberty.pe)

Cusco's elevation is approximately 3,400 meters/11,200 feet with about 35 percent less oxygen per breath than sea level, AMS symptoms typically appear within 24 to 48 hours, 2 to 3 days of acclimatization recommended before demanding excursions (voyagers.travel Cusco Elevation and Altitude Sickness; salkantaytrekking.com How to Acclimate in Cusco 2026)

Rail and road blockades tied to a dispute between bus concessionaires Consettur and San Antonio de Torontoy disrupted Machu Picchu access in September and November 2025, stranding about 900 tourists and prompting overnight evacuation trains for roughly 1,400 more, situation unresolved into early 2026 (adept.travel Machu Picchu Peru Protests Disrupt Trains And Buses; perurail.com protest updates page)

A common Cusco/Peru tourist scam involves people posing as plainclothes police asking to inspect cash for counterfeit bills, genuine police do not do this, official or app-based taxis (Uber, InDriver) with pre-agreed fares are recommended (theonlyperuguide.com Is Cusco Safe in 2026; beforeyougotravels.com Cusco safety assessment)

US, UK, Canadian, EU and Japanese citizens do not need a visa for Peru tourist visits, stays typically granted up to 90 days (max 183 days per 365-day period), passport must be valid 6+ months beyond departure, 2026 rules require visa-exempt travelers to complete electronic registration (TAM Virtual) at least 72 hours before arrival (southamerica.travel Peru Visa Requirements 2026; fertur-travel.com Complete Guide to Peru Entry Requirements)

Cusco dry season runs roughly May to September (peak crowds July to August), rainy season November to April with January and February the wettest and some treks closed for maintenance, late April to May and September to early October cited as calmer shoulder windows (fertur-travel.com Best Time to Visit Cusco; theonlyperuguide.com Best Time to Visit Cusco)

Qorikancha was the Inca empire's principal sun temple with gold-sheathed walls, later built over by a colonial church; Sacsayhuaman's fortress walls include stones weighing up to 200 tons; Ollantaytambo remains an inhabited 15th century town with its original stone street grid (peru-explorer.com; amautaspanish.com Best Inca Sites to Visit in Cusco)

Cusco's contemporary dining scene includes Gaston Acurio's restaurant Chicha and the contemporary Andean menu at MAP Cafe inside the Museo de Arte Precolombino, alongside traditional dishes like alpaca, cuy (guinea pig) and lomo saltado (theonlyperuguide.com Cusco Food Guide 2026)

destinations.name: Edinburgh
destinations.summary: A genuinely stunning, walkable capital with a castle, a volcano, and centuries of stone packed into a small footprint, undercut by a Royal Mile that has become one of the most-complained-about tourist traps in the UK, an August that triples hotel prices, and a new 5 percent visitor levy that just started.
destinations.headline: Edinburgh in 2026: gorgeous Old Town, brutal August pricing, a new 5% tourist tax, and a Royal Mile full of traps
destinations.body:
Edinburgh earns its reputation. The Old Town's medieval closes climb up from Princes Street toward a castle perched on an extinct volcano, and Arthur's Seat gives you a genuine hike with a summit view over the whole city, all within a 20 to 30 minute walk of the train station. It photographs as well as anywhere in Europe and it is compact enough to see the highlights on foot in two or three days. That said, treat any description of Edinburgh as effortlessly charming with suspicion, because a lot of the experience now depends on when you show up and how much you plan ahead.

As of 24 July 2026, Edinburgh became the first UK city to charge a visitor levy, a 5 percent surcharge added to paid overnight accommodation for the first five consecutive nights of a stay, projected to raise up to 50 million pounds a year for the city. It applies to bookings made on or after 1 October 2025, so anyone who paid for a stay before that date is exempt even if the trip itself falls in 2026. Budget for it the same way you would a hotel tax anywhere else, but do not be surprised if it appears as a separate line at checkout rather than folded into the quoted room rate.

Edinburgh Castle itself is worth the visit but no longer worth a walk-up ticket. It now runs on 30-minute timed-entry slots, adult online tickets run in the low-to-mid 20s in pounds (roughly 21 to 24 online, more at the gate), and booking online both saves a few pounds and is the only realistic way to guarantee a slot in July or August. Skipping the booking and just showing up in peak season is a good way to lose half a day.

August is the real trap for anyone budgeting loosely. The Fringe Festival runs 7 to 31 August 2026, and it turns Edinburgh into one of the most expensive small cities in Britain for those three and a half weeks. Hostel dorm beds that normally run 20 to 35 pounds jump to 45 to 80, budget chain hotels that are 55 to 140 pounds off-season climb to 150 to 300, and the well-located rooms are typically gone by January or February. If money matters, visit in the shoulder months instead. January through March and November offer 20 to 40 percent discounts on accommodation compared with summer, and the weather in July and August, while the warmest of the year at around 19C by day, still carries real rain risk and can turn cold and windy with little warning, especially up on Arthur's Seat or Calton Hill.

The Royal Mile is the other honest disappointment. It is genuinely picturesque and worth walking once, but it has been named repeatedly as one of the worst tourist traps in the UK, with hundreds of reviews flagging tacky souvenir shops and whisky stores that quote prices on the spot rather than posting them, sometimes well above what the same bottle costs elsewhere. There has also been a documented rise in shoplifting and theft targeting shops along the street, which locals have described as making parts of it feel poorly policed. None of that makes the street dangerous for visitors, but it does mean the tartan shops and whisky tastings closest to the castle are the least trustworthy version of what Scotland actually sells.

Any international visitor who is not a British or Irish citizen and does not already hold UK immigration status now needs a UK Electronic Travel Authorisation before arrival, a requirement that started 25 February 2026. It costs 20 pounds per person as of April 2026, up from 16 pounds, with no discount for children, and it is valid for up to two years. It is a five-minute online application but it is easy to forget since it is separate from a passport and from any US-style ESTA people may already be used to.
destinations.what_great: The Old Town skyline, the castle on its volcanic crag, and Arthur's Seat give Edinburgh a compact, walkable core where genuinely dramatic scenery sits a short walk from the train station, something few European capitals manage. Crime against tourists is low and violent crime is rare, with Police Scotland logging only 47 tourist-related thefts across all of 2025, and the city's museums, closes, and viewpoints reward slow wandering without needing a car or a big budget for entry fees.
destinations.what_ruined: The Royal Mile has curdled into one of the most complained-about tourist traps in the country, with unposted whisky prices and a documented rise in shop theft, and the city's calendar now punishes anyone who cannot travel in the shoulder season, since the Fringe from 7 to 31 August roughly doubles or triples accommodation costs and a new 5 percent visitor levy on top of already-rising hotel and bus fares adds friction that simply did not exist a couple of years ago.
tips: Book Edinburgh Castle online in advance: adult tickets run roughly 21 to 24 pounds online versus more at the gate, and entry is now assigned in 30-minute timed slots that sell out in July and August.

A new 5 percent visitor levy started 24 July 2026 on paid overnight stays for the first five nights; it applies only to bookings made on or after 1 October 2025, so factor it into any hotel quote from now on.

If you are not a British or Irish citizen and lack UK immigration status, apply for a UK ETA before you fly; it costs 20 pounds per person as of April 2026 and takes only minutes online, but it is separate from your passport and easy to forget.

Avoid the Royal Mile's whisky and tartan shops closest to the castle for actual purchases; prices are often quoted verbally rather than posted, and the street has documented theft and overcharging complaints. Buy whisky at a supermarket or a reputable specialist like Royal Mile Whiskies instead.

If the Fringe (7 to 31 August 2026) is not the specific draw, avoid it: budget hotel rates jump from roughly 55 to 140 pounds a night up to 150 to 300, and the best-located rooms are typically booked out by January or February.

Lothian Buses run a flat adult single fare of 2.20 pounds after the February 2026 fare revision, with a day ticket around 4.30 to 4.50 pounds, cheaper than the Airlink airport bus or tram for getting around once you are in the city.

From Edinburgh Airport, the tram runs 7.90 pounds one-way (9.50 pounds open return) and takes about 30 minutes to the city centre; the Airlink 100 bus is 6.00 pounds single (8.50 return), runs 24 hours including when the tram does not, but ask locally about journey time before assuming it is faster.

Visit in June through August for the warmest, driest weather (roughly 19C by day, around 70 to 83 mm of rain a month), or January through March for hotel rates 20 to 40 percent below summer if you can tolerate cold and rain.

guide.title: Edinburgh travel guide 2026: getting in, getting around, and dodging the Fringe-month price spike
guide.summary: A practical rundown of airport transfers, city transit, where to base yourself, and how to plan around the Fringe and the new visitor levy.
guide.body:
Edinburgh Airport sits about 8 miles west of the city centre and has three practical ways in. The tram is the simplest option for anyone staying near Princes Street or the Old Town: it runs directly from the airport concourse to York Place in about 30 minutes, costs 7.90 pounds for a single or 9.50 pounds for an open return, and departs every 7 minutes or so at peak times. The Airlink 100 bus is the budget and 24-hour option, running to Waverley Bridge for 6.00 pounds single or 8.50 pounds return, useful for late-night or early-morning arrivals when the tram is not running. Taxis cost considerably more but are worth it with heavy luggage or a group of three or four splitting the fare.

Once in the city, Edinburgh rewards walking. The Old Town and New Town sit close enough together that most first-time visitors barely need transit for sightseeing, but for anything further out, Lothian Buses run a flat adult single fare of 2.20 pounds citywide following the February 2026 fare revision, with an all-day ticket around 4.30 to 4.50 pounds that pays for itself after two rides. Cobblestones on the Royal Mile and steep closes off it are genuinely punishing in anything other than solid, flat shoes, worth knowing before you pack.

For where to stay, Old Town puts you inside the postcard view but means noise, tourist pricing, and the most theft-prone stretch of the Royal Mile on your doorstep. New Town, just across the valley from the castle, offers Georgian architecture, calmer streets, and easy tram or bus access at broadly similar prices. Leith, the old port district a short bus or tram ride north, has become the value and food-scene alternative, generally 15 to 30 percent cheaper for comparable rooms with a 10 to 15 minute commute into the centre.

If your trip falls anywhere near 7 to 31 August 2026, plan around the Fringe deliberately rather than by accident. It is genuinely one of the world's great arts festivals and worth experiencing once, but budget hotel rates that normally run 55 to 140 pounds a night jump to 150 to 300, mid-range hotels roughly double, and the best-located rooms are typically gone by January or February of that year. Either book seriously early, accept a base outside the centre with a transit commute, or deliberately avoid the dates if a lower-key, cheaper Edinburgh is the goal, shoulder months like May, June, September, or the discounted window of January through March are all reasonable substitutes.

For day trips, Glasgow is the easy one: ScotRail runs direct trains every 15 to 20 minutes between Edinburgh Waverley and Glasgow Queen Street, taking roughly 50 minutes with fares as low as 8.40 pounds one-way if booked ahead. Highlands day tours by coach run considerably longer, 12 hours or more round trip, and are worth it only if a full Highlands trip is not otherwise on the itinerary. On money matters generally, contactless and Apple/Google Pay are accepted almost everywhere including on Lothian Buses, so carrying cash is mostly unnecessary except for the odd small independent shop.

rating_rationale.overall: The core sights, castle, Old Town, Arthur's Seat, are legitimately excellent and easy to reach on foot, but a tourist-trap-heavy Royal Mile and a festival month that reshapes pricing and crowding for a third of the summer keep it from a top score.
rating_rationale.safety: Police Scotland's own 2025 numbers show only 47 tourist-related thefts citywide for the year and violent crime against visitors is rare; pickpocketing in crowded spots like the Royal Mile and Waverley Station is the main real risk, not personal safety.
rating_rationale.value: Outside August, mid-range hotels run roughly 120 to 175 pounds a night and city buses are a flat 2.20 pounds a ride, reasonable for a UK capital, but Fringe-month pricing that can triple room rates plus the new 5 percent visitor levy and rising transit fares pull the average down.

facts_checked: Edinburgh visitor levy: 5% surcharge on paid overnight accommodation for first 5 consecutive nights, took effect 24 July 2026, applies to bookings made on/after 1 October 2025, projected to raise up to £50m/year, Edinburgh first UK city to introduce one — https://www.indexbox.io/blog/edinburgh-introduces-5-tourist-tax-on-overnight-stays-from-24-july-2026/ and https://geniustravels.co.uk/travel-news/edinburgh-tourist-tax-2026/

Edinburgh Castle adult ticket ~£21.50-23.50 online (more at gate), 30-minute timed entry slots, booking online saves ~£2 — https://tripscot.co.uk/budget/edinburgh-castle-tickets and https://thebettervacation.com/edinburgh/edinburgh-castle-tickets/

UK ETA required from 25 February 2026 for non-British/Irish nationals without UK immigration status; fee raised from £16 to £20 on 8 April 2026; valid up to 2 years; no family/child discount — https://etavisauk.org/en/uk-eta-2026-rules-cost-2/ and https://arlettipartners.com/uk-eta-cost-to-rise-from-april-2026/
Edinburgh Festival Fringe 2026 runs 7-31 August 2026 — https://festivalcalendar.uk/edinburgh-fringe/

Festival-month accommodation surge: hostel dorms £45-80 (vs £20-35 normal), budget hotels £150-300 (vs £55-140 normal), mid-range £250-500 (vs £140-280), best rooms gone by Jan/Feb — https://www.edinburghtourism.org/edinburgh-festival-accommodation/

Lothian Buses adult single fare rose 20p to £2.20 and day ticket rose 50p (~£4.30-4.50) in fare revision effective 22 February 2026 — https://www.lothianbuses.com/news/2026/01/fares-revision/ and https://feeds.bbci.co.uk/news/articles/cn48l83ej7jo
Edinburgh Trams airport-to-city single fare £7.90 (frozen for 2026), open return £9.50, ~30 minute journey to York Place — https://edinburghtrams.com/news/changes-tram-fares-2026
Airlink 100 airport bus adult single £6.00, open return £8.50, buses run 24 hours — https://www.lothianbuses.com/our-services/airport-buses/

Edinburgh July average ~19C day/12C night with ~83mm rain; August ~19C day/11C night with ~70mm rain; June-August cited as best weather window — https://weather-and-climate.com/Edinburgh-uk-July-averages and https://weather-and-climate.com/average-monthly-Rainfall-Temperature-Sunshine,Edinburgh-uk,Scotland

Royal Mile named one of world's worst tourist traps in TripAdvisor review analysis (539 reviews mention 'tourist trap'); whisky shops accused of quoting unposted prices on the spot; documented shoplifting/theft 'epidemic' of cashmere, tweed and whisky prompting calls for more police presence — https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/community/edinburgh-street-revealed-as-one-of-the-worlds-worst-tourist-traps-5222387 and https://news.stv.tv/east-central/thieves-steal-cashmere-and-whisky-as-staff-left-afraid-on-lawless-royal-mile

Edinburgh composite safety score 21/100 (low risk); Police Scotland logged 47 tourist-related thefts in 2025, down from 62 in 2024; pickpocketing is most common crime, violent crime against tourists rare — https://www.travelriskcalculator.com/destinations/united-kingdom/edinburgh

Arthur's Seat: common injuries are twisted ankles and slips on wet rock; summit 5-10C cooler and windier than city centre; a wildfire broke out on Arthur's Seat/Holyrood Park on 19 July 2026 closing the area; a prior August 2025 fire closed the High Road for 10 weeks — https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/20/uk/edinburgh-scotland-wildfire-scli-intl and https://uprootedtraveler.com/arthurs-seat-hike/

Non-festival mid-range hotel rates roughly £120-175/night; January cheapest month (~$162 avg); January-March and November offer 20-40% discounts vs summer/Christmas — https://hotelmonitor.co.uk/hotels/edinburgh/october-2026 and https://www.edinburghtourism.org/cheap-accommodation-edinburgh/

Edinburgh Waverley to Glasgow Queen Street direct ScotRail trains every 15-20 minutes, ~50 minute journey, fares from £8.40 one-way — https://www.scotrail.co.uk/train-times/edinburgh-waverley-to-glasgow-queen-street and https://www.omio.co.uk/trains/edinburgh/glasgow

destinations.name: Hoi An
destinations.summary: UNESCO-listed Vietnamese trading port on the Thu Bon river, known for tailors, lantern nights and heavy autumn flooding. Small, walkable, heavily touristed.
destinations.headline: Hoi An Review: A Genuinely Beautiful Old Town With a Tailor-Shop Hustle and a Flood Season
destinations.body:
Hoi An sits on the Thu Bon river in Quang Nam province, roughly 30 kilometres south of Da Nang, and it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List on December 4, 1999 as an exceptionally well preserved Southeast Asian trading port of the 15th to 19th centuries. That listing is earned. The Ancient Town core, essentially Tran Phu, Nguyen Thai Hoc and Bach Dang streets, is a dense grid of ochre shophouses, Chinese assembly halls and the Japanese Covered Bridge, known locally as Chua Cau, which reopened in early August 2024 after a two year restoration costing about 20.2 billion Vietnamese dong, funded equally by Quang Nam province and Hoi An city. The rebuilt bridge drew public criticism for looking too new, and visitors expecting a weathered 400 year old structure should reset expectations.

Access to the heritage core runs on a ticket. Foreign visitors pay 120,000 VND, sold at the small yellow booths at the main entrances, valid 24 hours, and the ticket covers entry to five of the 22 listed heritage buildings, with a tear off strip surrendered at each door. Street level enforcement is inconsistent and many people wander the lanes without buying, but every assembly hall, old house and museum checks it at the door.

Arrival is simple. Da Nang International Airport is the gateway, about 45 minutes out. Grab runs roughly 250,000 to 350,000 VND, plus a small airport pickup surcharge paid directly to the driver, metered taxis land around 300,000 to 400,000 VND, and prearranged private cars sit at 350,000 to 500,000 VND. Touts working the arrivals hall quote 500,000 to 700,000 VND for the identical trip, so use the app or the official rank and decline everything else.

Timing decides the quality of the visit. February to April is the dependable window, warm and dry with low humidity. May to August stays dry but gets genuinely punishing, with highs approaching 40C. September to November is typhoon and flood season on the central coast, and this is not an abstraction. On October 30, 2025 the Thu Bon crested at 5.62 metres in Hoi An, 14 centimetres above the 1964 record, and water only drained out of the Ancient Town on October 31, leaving thick mud through the shophouses. Bach Dang, Nguyen Thai Hoc and Tran Phu, the exact streets visitors come for, sit lowest and flood first. November 2025 brought a second round of inundation.

The lantern night, Dem Ram Pho Co, falls on the 14th night of each lunar month. Remaining 2026 dates include 27 July, 26 August, 24 September, 23 October, 22 November and 22 December. Motorbikes are cleared from the core around 5:30 pm, electric lighting goes down between roughly 6 and 10 pm, and the candle boat release on the Hoai river peaks between 7 and 9 pm.

Outside town, My Son Sanctuary, the Cham temple complex about 50 kilometres inland, charges 150,000 VND for foreigners, which covers the site museum, the electric shuttle to the temple groups and the traditional dance performance.

The honest caveat is commerce. Tailoring is Hoi An's signature industry and also its best documented problem. Hotel staff, drivers and friendly strangers routinely collect 20 to 40 percent commission for delivering a customer to a particular shop, and that cut comes out of either the price or the garment. Suits quoted under 100 US dollars are typically fused rather than canvassed, and synthetic blends are regularly sold to visitors as mulberry silk. A suit promised in 24 hours is usually a modified off the rack piece from a volume factory. None of this makes Hoi An a bad destination. It makes it a place where the visitor who books a tailor directly, allows three or four days for real fittings, and treats the first quoted number as an opening position ends up with a completely different trip from the one who does not.
destinations.what_great: The heritage core is the real thing, a dense grid of 15th to 19th century shophouses and Chinese assembly halls on Tran Phu and Nguyen Thai Hoc that earned UNESCO listing in December 1999. The scale is walkable and bicycle friendly, with An Bang beach a flat 10 to 20 minute ride away. Lantern nights on the 14th of each lunar month shut the core to traffic and kill the electric lighting between roughly 6 and 10 pm. My Son Sanctuary is a legitimate half day at 150,000 VND.
destinations.what_ruined: Tailoring runs on commission, with hotel staff, drivers and strangers taking 20 to 40 percent for steering you to a shop, money that comes straight out of fabric quality. Suits under 100 dollars are fused, polyester is sold as mulberry silk, and 24 hour turnaround means factory garments. Airport touts quote 500,000 to 700,000 VND for a 300,000 VND ride. September to November is flood season: the Thu Bon hit a record 5.62 metres on October 30, 2025, and flooded again in November. Foreigner pricing is routine.
tips: Buy the Ancient Town ticket at the yellow booths for 120,000 VND; it is valid 24 hours and covers five of the 22 listed heritage buildings via tear-off coupons.
Book a tailor yourself rather than through your hotel or driver, because the referral commission of 20 to 40 percent comes out of your fabric quality or your price.
Aim for February to April, when central Vietnam is warm and dry, and avoid September to November, when the Thu Bon flooded to a record 5.62 metres on October 30, 2025.
From Da Nang airport use Grab at roughly 250,000 to 350,000 VND plus a small airport pickup surcharge, and refuse touts quoting 500,000 to 700,000 VND.
Time your visit to a lantern night on the 14th of the lunar month, with 2026 dates including 24 September and 23 October, when motorbikes clear around 5:30 pm and lights go off from about 6 to 10 pm.
Budget a full 150,000 VND for the My Son Sanctuary ticket, which already covers the site museum, the electric shuttle and the Cham dance performance, and go at opening to beat the heat.

guide.title: Hoi An Practical Guide: Tickets, Da Nang Transfers, Flood Months and Tailor Rules
guide.summary: Month by month timing, real Da Nang airport transfer costs, current Ancient Town and My Son ticket prices, daily budget bands, and how the tailor commission system actually works.
guide.body:
When to go is the single decision that matters most in Hoi An. February through April is the strongest window, with warm days, low humidity and very little rain. May through August is reliably dry but hot, with central Vietnam highs pushing toward 40C, which makes midday walking through the Ancient Town unpleasant and pushes most activity to early morning and after dark. September through November is typhoon and flood season on the central coast and is the period to avoid if the trip is inflexible. The 2025 season was the clearest possible illustration: the Thu Bon river reached 5.62 metres in Hoi An on October 30, 2025, 14 centimetres higher than the 1964 record, floodwater sat in the Ancient Town until October 31, and a second round of flooding hit in early November. December and January are cooler and drier than October and November but still fall inside the wet season, so beach days are unreliable.

Getting in means Da Nang International Airport, roughly 30 kilometres and about 45 minutes north. Grab is the cleanest option at roughly 250,000 to 350,000 VND, with a small airport pickup surcharge handed to the driver on top of the in app fare. A metered taxi from the official rank, Mai Linh among them, generally runs 300,000 to 400,000 VND. A prearranged private transfer or hotel car costs 350,000 to 500,000 VND and is worth it on a late arrival. Freelance touts inside and outside arrivals quote 500,000 to 700,000 VND for the same ride. Decline them, walk to the rank, or open the app.

Getting around town is deliberately easy. The Ancient Town is small and closed to motorbikes during the pedestrian hours, so bicycles, usually free from hotels, cover almost everything including the 10 to 20 minute flat ride east to An Bang and Cua Dai beaches. Grab bikes and cars work for longer runs.

For sites, start with the Ancient Town ticket itself: 120,000 VND for foreigners, sold at yellow booths at the main entrances, valid 24 hours, admitting you to five of the 22 listed heritage buildings via tear off coupons. Spend the coupons on the assembly halls and old merchant houses rather than the smallest museums. The Japanese Covered Bridge, Chua Cau, reopened in August 2024 after a restoration costing about 20.2 billion VND, and it is worth seeing while accepting that the finish is visibly new and has been publicly criticised for exactly that. My Son Sanctuary, about 50 kilometres inland, charges 150,000 VND for foreigners, which includes the site museum, the electric shuttle and the dance show, and is best done on an early morning departure before the heat and the tour buses converge. Try to line the trip up with a lantern night, Dem Ram Pho Co, on the 14th night of the lunar month, with 2026 dates including 27 July, 26 August, 24 September, 23 October, 22 November and 22 December: motorbikes clear around 5:30 pm, electric lights go off from roughly 6 to 10 pm, and candle boats peak on the water between 7 and 9 pm. The one thing worth skipping is any tailor visit arranged by a driver or hotel desk.

On budget, the fixed and verifiable costs are modest. The Ancient Town ticket is 120,000 VND, My Son is 150,000 VND, and the airport transfer is 250,000 to 500,000 VND each way. At roughly 25,000 VND to the US dollar, that is about 5 dollars, 6 dollars and 10 to 20 dollars respectively. Around those numbers, a realistic all in daily figure is about 35 to 55 dollars for a budget traveller in a guesthouse eating at street stalls and local markets, about 70 to 120 dollars for a mid range visitor in a boutique hotel with sit down meals and a day trip, and 200 dollars and up if a tailored wardrobe or a riverside resort enters the picture. Treat clothing as a separate line, not a daily one.

Hoi An sees very little violent crime, so the safety conversation here is really about scams and weather, not personal danger. The commission system is the core issue: hotel staff, taxi drivers and helpful strangers earn 20 to 40 percent for steering customers to specific tailors, and that money comes out of fabric quality or your price. Suits under 100 dollars are fused rather than canvassed, polyester is sold as mulberry silk, and 24 hour turnaround means a factory made garment altered to fit. Book tailors independently, insist on multiple fittings across three or four days, and pay a deposit rather than the full amount up front. Agree fares before riding with non metered drivers, expect a foreigner price on unlabelled market goods, and during flood months check river conditions before committing to a riverside hotel.

rating_rationale.overall: The Ancient Town is a genuinely intact 15th to 19th century trading port with UNESCO inscription since December 1999, but the tailoring and souvenir economy is intense enough to shape the whole experience.
rating_rationale.safety: Violent crime is not the concern here; the real hazards are commercial pressure and a documented flood season, including the October 30, 2025 Thu Bon crest of 5.62 metres that put the Ancient Town underwater.
rating_rationale.value: Core costs are low, with a 120,000 VND Ancient Town ticket, a 150,000 VND My Son entry and a roughly 250,000 to 350,000 VND Grab from Da Nang airport, though commission-driven tailoring can inflate a trip quickly.

facts_checked.fact: Hoi An Ancient Town inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List on 4 December 1999 as a preserved 15th-19th century Southeast Asian trading port.
